system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for the Wattlebridge Holdings deal team. Seller materials treated as adverse drafting and tested against the Buyer Playbook. Format per issue: **Seller position → Buyer position → Recommendation (reason)**.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- *Buyer:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is our conditional fallback only, requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft; none exists.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** Seller has landed on our unauthorised fallback – conceding it now gives away the fallback for nothing and exceeds our mandate.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery.
- *Buyer:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the excess-only structure would absorb AUD 250k of loss outright – a second, hidden cap.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months, plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- *Buyer:* 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (not given).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject 18 months; hold at 24 months; delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** The default-application wording would silently pull fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims into the 18-month window (see N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer:* Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six-year period, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" would cap recovery for a total title failure at 20% of a price paid for 100% of the shares.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out appears.
- *Buyer:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable.
- *Recommendation:* **Insist on express carve-out as a non-negotiable.** As drafted the Seller would be contractually shielded from its own fraud – unacceptable and likely unenforceable, but we should not rely on a court to fix it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* Sch 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records; DL [1.4] reserves all admissions.
- *Buyer:* Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject [1.1]–[1.2]; require matters to be fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope.** Whole-room disclosure would qualify every warranty by every document, gutting the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- *Buyer:* Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer persons after reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that combined with N-006 would make the warranties unclaimable.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of written consent. DL [2] confirms no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- *Buyer:* Condition precedent requiring effective consent AND evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a ~30% / AUD 3.6m revenue customer.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; redraft as a hard CP with condition-satisfaction evidence.** A consent whose conditions are unmet is not an effective consent, and the Seller's own letter admits neither is in hand.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by a release "following Completion." DL [3] confirms no repayment and no discharge.
- *Buyer:* Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject post-completion release; require payout letter, funds-flow line and executed releases at Completion.** Debt-free/cash-free pricing is meaningless if we complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still in the target.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL [5] is silent on on-costs.
- *Buyer:* AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or otherwise seller-funded.
- *Recommendation:* **Require express funds-flow line (gross of on-costs) or a price adjustment/indemnity.** Bonuses triggered by Completion and continued employment will fall on the Company – i.e. on us – post-Completion unless expressly funded by the Seller.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate." DL [4]: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- *Buyer:* Broaden the indemnity to cover failure of title/transfer of SOW3 Project Materials and consequential loss, while preserving the cure (payment → transfer). Treat AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- *Recommendation:* **Broaden to cover ownership and transfer of the Project Materials, not just the payment; require pre-Completion payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as a CP or Completion deliverable.** The risk is loss of IP, not merely a AUD 180k invoice.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. DL [6]: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined.
- *Buyer:* Log preservation, completed investigation, periodic updates, cooperation covenants and a specific indemnity for liabilities arising from the incident. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum in either direction.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "not material" characterisation; require preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity.** The Seller's own letter says the facts are not yet known – which is exactly why it cannot be dismissed as immaterial.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- *Seller:* Three AUD 110,000 renewals (DD-008/DD-011) are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL [8]: silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Buyer:* Assess on the facts; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- *Recommendation:* **Hold – request renewal terms, timing and termination rights before accepting the ordinary-course label.** The Seller asserts a conclusion its own disclosure declines to support.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"; limitations apply to "all Claims"; fundamental warranties folded into general caps.
- *Buyer:* Title/Tax/IP/payment obligations/covenants kept as separate regimes with their own caps and periods; no general-regime override.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject every default-application clause; add an express priority clause that specific regimes prevail.** The draft uses three separate provisions to achieve the same override – it is a structural device, not a drafting accident.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL [10] concedes this is merely the source relied on and no Buyer verification has been done.
- *Buyer:* Independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances and authority (ASIC search, PPSR search, share certificates, board approvals, constitution compliance) plus unlimited title warranty.
- *Recommendation:* **Require independent title and encumbrance evidence as a Completion deliverable; do not accept DD-012 as proof.** An internal register supplied by the Seller is the Seller's own assertion – especially relevant given Riverlark's security.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranties "settled" under the general regime.
- *Buyer:* Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; separate regimes to be negotiated; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- *Recommendation:* **Mark as open; reject the "settled" characterisation in writing.** Silence could be read as acquiescence to a 20%/18-month tax and IP regime.

---

### Summary for the deal team
Nothing in this draft is acceptable as sent. The core concern is cumulative: whole-data-room disclosure (N-006) + constructive buyer knowledge (N-007) + general-regime override (N-003/004/014/016) + no fraud carve-out (N-005) would together make the warranty package largely illusory. Separately, the three Completion-mechanics items (N-008 Bluefen, N-009 Riverlark, N-010 bonuses) go to whether we actually receive what we are paying AUD 24m for. **No authority exists for any fallback used in this draft; all positions should be held at playbook baseline pending Amelia Frost's direction.**
=== END ADVICE ===
